nodes.description: Biallelic mutations in TTPA cause loss or severe reduction of hepatic alpha-tocopherol transfer protein (alpha-TTP) activity. Because alpha-TTP is responsible for selectively binding diet-derived RRR-alpha-tocopherol in hepatocytes and facilitating its transfer into nascent VLDL particles, its deficiency impairs hepatic vitamin E retention and recycling while intestinal absorption via chylomicrons remains intact.

nodes.description: Lifelong daily oral administration of high-dose vitamin E (typically 800-1500 mg/day or 40 mg/kg/day in children in divided doses) to restore plasma alpha-tocopherol concentrations to the high-normal range. Initiated presymptomatically, it completely prevents neurological manifestations; initiated early in symptomatic patients, it halts disease progression and can partially reverse ataxia and neurological deficits.

evidence.snippet: Lifelong targeted therapy with high-dose oral vitamin E supplementation (that brings plasma vitamin E concentrations into the high-normal range) initiated in presymptomatic individuals (e.g., younger sibs of an index case) prevents the manifestations of AVED. Vitamin E supplementation early in the disease course of a symptomatic individual may to some extent reverse ataxia and mental deterioration.
